name: Trump Organization

summary.text: The Trump Organization is the privately held real-estate and licensing business of the Trump family; Eric Trump is its executive vice president. In 2024-26 it announced a series of branded projects in the Gulf with the Saudi-backed developer Dar Global: Trump Tower Jeddah (December 2024), Trump International Hotel & Tower Dubai (April 30, 2025), Trump International Golf Club and villas at Simaisma in Qatar with Qatari Diar, a subsidiary of the Qatar Investment Authority (April 30, 2025), Trump Plaza Jeddah (September 2025) and a golf project in Diriyah, Riyadh (January 2026). Separately, in May 2025 the Pentagon accepted a Boeing 747-8 from the government of Qatar for modification as a presidential aircraft, which Democratic members of Congress challenged under the Foreign Emoluments Clause, and the White House published fact sheets on investment pledges from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE during the president's May 2025 trip.

sources.title: Qatari Diar Signs Strategic Agreement with Dar Global to Develop Trump International Golf Club and Trump Villas

Trump Attempts To Make Good On His Proposal For A Middle Eastern Riviera — But In Dubai, Jeddah, And Riyadh

facts.claim: On April 30, 2025, Qatari Diar and Dar Global signed an agreement at Qatari Diar's headquarters in Lusail to develop Trump International Golf Club and Trump-branded villas within the Simaisma master plan, 40 kilometres north of Doha, with an 18-hole course and clubhouse on about 790,000 square metres. Qatari Diar's website states it was established in 2005 by the Qatar Investment Authority. Qatari Diar's CEO Ali Mohamed Al-Ali said the partnership was expected to bring about $2 billion in foreign investment into Qatar.
facts.quote: The project is part of the landmark Simaisma coastal project located 40 kilometres north of Doha.

sources.title: Qatari Diar Signs Strategic Agreement with Dar Global to Develop Trump International Golf Club and Trump Villas
Qatari Diar Partners with Dar Global to Develop Trump International Golf Club, Trump Villas
About Qatari Diar

facts.claim: Eric Trump, executive vice president of the Trump Organization, said of the Qatar agreement: 'We are incredibly proud to expand the Trump brand into Qatar through this exceptional collaboration with Qatari Diar and Dar Global.'
facts.quote: We are incredibly proud to expand the Trump brand into Qatar through this exceptional collaboration with Qatari Diar and Dar Global. Trump International Golf Club Simaisma and our luxury villa community will reflect our highest standards of quality, prestige, and timeless elegance.

sources.title: Qatari Diar Signs Strategic Agreement with Dar Global to Develop Trump International Golf Club and Trump Villas
Dar Global and The Trump Organization Expand Partnership with New Luxury Golf and Villa Project within Simaisma Masterplan

facts.claim: On April 30, 2025, Dar Global and the Trump Organization announced the launch of Trump International Hotel & Tower Dubai, an 80-floor, 350-metre tower on Sheikh Zayed Road at the entrance of Downtown Dubai, described as the fifth collaboration between the two companies. Dar Global had first announced a Trump tower in Dubai in July 2024.
facts.quote: It is the Middle East's first and only Trump International Hotel & Tower and the fifth collaboration between DarGlobal and the Trump Organisation.

sources.title: DarGlobal and The Trump Organization Launch Dubai's New Icon, Trump International Hotel & Tower
Dar Global and The Trump Organization Launch Dubai's New Icon, Trump International Hotel & Tower
Dar Global Announces Third Collaboration With Trump Organization to Launch Iconic Trump Tower Dubai in 2025

facts.claim: In Saudi Arabia, the Trump Organization and Dar Global launched Trump Tower Jeddah, a 47-storey residential tower on the Jeddah Corniche, in December 2024, with completion planned for December 2029; announced Trump Plaza Jeddah, a mixed-use project within the Amaya development on King Abdulaziz Road, in September 2025; and in January 2026 announced a Trump International Golf Club in Wadi Safar within the Diriyah master plan near Riyadh, on a site of 2.6 million square metres. Reuters, cited by The National, put the combined value of the Diriyah and Jeddah projects at $10 billion.
facts.quote: Spread across 2.6 million square metres will be the Trump International Golf Club in Wadi Safar, the master plan being developed by Diriyah Company.

sources.title: Dar Global and Trump Organisation launch luxury project in Riyadh's Diriyah
Dar Global announces Trump-branded Jeddah project
Elegance in the Sky: DarGlobal and Trump Organization Unveil Jeddah Tower

facts.claim: On May 21, 2025, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell announced that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had accepted a Boeing 747 from Qatar, stating: 'The Secretary of Defense has accepted a Boeing 747 from Qatar in accordance with all federal rules and regulations.' The Air Force said it was preparing to award a contract to convert the 747-8 into a presidential transport and that the contract details were classified. The aircraft was valued in reporting at about $400 million.
facts.quote: The Secretary of Defense has accepted a Boeing 747 from Qatar in accordance with all federal rules and regulations.

sources.title: Pentagon accepts Qatari jet for Air Force One
Pentagon accepts luxury jet from Qatar to use as Air Force One
Pentagon accepts Qatari jet to use as Air Force One

facts.claim: The Air Force's first public statement on the Qatari 747-8 said the aircraft was being modified for 'Executive Airlift support' and that contract details were classified, declining to name the contractor or scope of work. In January 2026 the Air Force said it anticipated delivery of the 'VC-25 bridge aircraft' no later than summer 2026, and in May 2026 it said the jet had completed modification and flight testing and that L3Harris Technologies had been selected to modify it in collaboration with Boeing. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said the retrofit would probably cost less than $400 million; critics in Congress said the cost would approach $1 billion.
facts.quote: The Air Force remains committed to expediting delivery of the VC-25 bridge aircraft in support of the Presidential airlift mission, with an anticipated delivery no later than summer 2026.

sources.title: USAF Starts Modifying 747 to Serve as Air Force One
Qatari jet-turned-Air Force One expected to be delivered this summer, Air Force says
Air Force says former Qatari 747 will be ready to fly as Air Force One this summer

facts.claim: Democratic members of Congress challenged the Qatari aircraft as a foreign emolument. On May 14, 2025 Senate Judiciary ranking member Dick Durbin asked Attorney General Pam Bondi for the Justice Department memo reportedly finding the gift 'legally permissible'; on May 15, 2025 Rep. Jamie Raskin and other House Judiciary Democrats wrote to Bondi and White House Counsel David Warrington; Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer placed a hold on Justice Department nominees; and S.Res.244 would declare acceptance of the plane without Congress's consent an illegal emolument. These are allegations and requests by members of Congress, not findings.
facts.quote: affirming that the underlying purpose of the Foreign Emoluments Clause renders the acceptance and transfer of a plane from the Government of Qatar, without the explicit consent of Congress, an illegal emolument

sources.url: https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/2025-05-14 Letter to DOJ Qatari Plane Gift.pdf
sources.title: Letter to DOJ on Qatari Plane Gift
Raskin et al. to Bondi (DOJ) and Warrington (WHCO) re Qatar Plane Emolument

Records request regarding the Qatari plane

facts.claim: During the president's May 2025 trip to the Gulf, the White House published fact sheets stating that Saudi Arabia had committed to invest $600 billion in the United States (May 13), that the president had signed an agreement with Qatar to generate an economic exchange worth at least $1.2 trillion, including deals totalling more than $243.5 billion (May 14), and that the UAE had agreed to more than $200 billion in new deals while accelerating a previously committed $1.4 trillion investment (May 15). The figures are the administration's announced headline values.
facts.quote: The May 15 announcement covered over $200 billion in commercial deals, bringing total investment agreements in the Gulf region to over $2 trillion.

sources.title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Secures Historic $600 Billion Investment Commitment in Saudi Arabia
Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Secures Historic $1.2 Trillion Economic Commitment in Qatar
Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Secures $200 Billion in New U.S.-UAE Deals and Accelerates Previously Committed $1.4 Trillion UAE Investment

facts.claim: A January 4, 2024 report by the Democratic staff of the House Oversight Committee, 'White House for Sale', concluded that Trump-owned businesses received at least $7.8 million from 20 foreign governments and government-backed entities during his presidency, based on 451 pages of records mainly from the former accounting firm Mazars USA. The analysis covered four properties (Trump International Hotel Washington, Trump International Hotel Las Vegas, Trump Tower and Trump World Tower) and only part of the term, and the authors said the total was likely incomplete. It is a minority-staff report, not a committee finding.
facts.quote: Democratic staffers on the House Oversight Committee on Thursday issued their 156-page report, and the payments came from foreign governments and government-backed entities from 20 countries.

sources.title: White House for Sale: How Princes, Prime Ministers, and Premiers Paid Off President Trump
Trump's businesses got at least $7.8 million in foreign payments while he was president, House Democrats say

facts.claim: The Oversight Democratic staff report identified China as the largest source of the foreign payments it traced, about $5.5 million, including payments from China's embassy in the United States, the state-owned Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and Hainan Airlines; Saudi Arabia was second with more than $615,000 at Trump World Tower and the Trump International Hotel in Washington.
facts.quote: China made the largest total payment to Trump's properties, amounting to $5.5 million including millions from China's U.S. Embassy, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and Hainan Airlines Holding Company.

sources.title: White House for Sale: How Princes, Prime Ministers, and Premiers Paid Off President Trump
Trump's businesses got at least $7.8 million in foreign payments while he was president, House Democrats say

facts.claim: The Trump Organization responded that 'the vast majority' of the payments identified came from leases entered before Trump became president and that it had donated profits from foreign-government stays to the Treasury; Eric Trump told the New York Times 'That narrative is insane.' Ranking member Jamie Raskin wrote to the company on January 12 and January 21, 2024 rejecting those defences.
facts.quote: Trump's side has argued that "the vast majority" of the payments came from leases the Trump Organization entered before he became President.

sources.title: Letter from Ranking Member Raskin to the Trump Organization regarding its emoluments response
Trump's businesses got at least $7.8 million in foreign payments while he was president, House Democrats say

facts.claim: On January 25, 2021, the Supreme Court vacated the lower-court rulings in the Foreign Emoluments Clause suits brought by the District of Columbia and Maryland (over the Trump International Hotel in Washington) and by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (over Trump's New York hotels), and sent the cases back with instructions to dismiss them as moot because Trump had left office. The cases were never decided on the merits.
facts.quote: The high court sent the cases, brought by a government watchdog group and the attorneys general of Maryland and the District of Columbia, back to the lower courts with instructions to dismiss them as moot.

sources.title: Supreme Court tosses emoluments cases against Trump
Supreme Court Gutters Emoluments Cases Against Trump

facts.claim: The Trump Organization held a 60-year lease from the General Services Administration on the federally owned Old Post Office building in Washington, operated as the Trump International Hotel. In November 2021 it agreed to sell the lease to Miami-based CGI Merchant Group, which planned to remove the Trump name and rebrand the hotel as a Waldorf Astoria; GSA approval was required. The price was reported at $375 million by people familiar with the deal; the hotel was reported to have lost more than $70 million during the four years of the presidency.
facts.quote: The Trump Organization has reached a deal with the investment fund CGI Merchant Group to purchase the lease for the Trump International Hotel in Washington, DC, for $375 million.

sources.title: CGI Merchant Group purchases Trump hotel in DC; expected to remove Trump name
Trump Organization to sell Washington hotel for $375 million: Report

facts.claim: In May 2022 the Trump Organization announced it had completed the sale of the Trump International Hotel Washington lease to CGI Merchant Group of Miami, describing the price as a record per room for the city; the $375 million figure came from sources close to the deal rather than a filing.
facts.quote: The Trump Organization said Wednesday it had completed the sale of the Trump International Hotel to CGI Merchant Group of Miami for what it described as a record price per room for the city.

sources.title: Trump Organization Completes $375 million Sale of D.C. Hotel

facts.claim: After the Small Business Administration released Paycheck Protection Program recipient data in December 2020, an NBC News analysis found that businesses located at properties owned by the Trump Organization and by Jared Kushner's family companies received more than two dozen PPP loans worth more than $3.65 million, including a $2,164,543 loan to Triomphe Restaurant Corp. at the Trump International Hotel & Tower in New York, which reported retaining no jobs. The loans went to tenants, not to the Trump or Kushner companies themselves. Kushner Companies' general counsel called any suggestion of improper benefit 'completely untrue'.
facts.quote: businesses at properties owned by the Trump Organization and President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner's family reportedly received more than two dozen Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans worth more than $3.65 million.

sources.title: Trump Organization, Kushner Companies benefited from pandemic relief loans: report
Over $3.65 Million in PPP Loans Given to Businesses With Ties to Trump Organization, Kushner Properties

facts.claim: PolitiFact, citing ProPublica's July 2020 reporting on the first PPP data release, recorded that Kushner-family-linked companies received PPP loans disclosed in ranges, including $350,000 to $1 million for Observer Holdings LLC and $1 million to $2 million for Princeton Forrestal LLC; the SBA published amounts in brackets rather than exact figures at that stage.
facts.quote: PolitiFact reports that several Kushner-linked companies received PPP money, with loan ranges such as between $350,000 and $1 million for Observer Holdings LLC and between $1 million and $2 million for Princeton Forrestal LLC.

sources.title: Fact-checking which Trump supporters and allies got PPP loans

facts.claim: The New Yorker (Adam Davidson, March 2017) reported that the Trump International Hotel & Tower Baku, conceived in 2008 as an apartment building, became a Trump-branded project in 2012 after the Trump Organization signed multiple contracts with its Azerbaijani developers, members of the Mammadov family; the building had not opened, and the Trump Organization later withdrew from the deal.
facts.quote: In 2012, after Donald Trump's company, the Trump Organization, signed multiple contracts with the Azerbaijani developers behind the project, plans were made to transform the tower into an ultra-luxury property.

sources.publisher: Reader Supported News (reprint of The New Yorker, Adam Davidson)
sources.title: Donald Trump's Worst Deal
'The New Yorker' Uncovers Trump Hotel's Ties To Corrupt Oligarch Family

facts.claim: NPR summarized the New Yorker report as finding that the Baku partners, the Mammadov family, were described by a U.S. diplomat as notoriously corrupt and had done business with companies linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guard; the article characterized the project as apparently corrupt. These are the reporter's characterizations, not findings of wrongdoing against the Trump Organization.
facts.quote: Davidson writes that Trump did business with corrupt partners who also did business with Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

sources.title: 'The New Yorker' Uncovers Trump Hotel's Ties To Corrupt Oligarch Family

sources.publisher: Reader Supported News (reprint of The New Yorker, Adam Davidson)
sources.title: Donald Trump's Worst Deal

facts.claim: In March 2017 Senators Sherrod Brown, Ben Cardin and Dianne Feinstein wrote to the Treasury Secretary, the Attorney General and the FBI Director citing the New Yorker article and asking for an investigation of the Trump Organization's Baku dealings; the letter stated that the organization appeared to have withdrawn from the Baku Tower deal but that questions about potential liability remained.
facts.quote: Even though the Trump Organization appears to have withdrawn from the Baku Tower deal, serious questions remain unanswered about the Trump Organization's potential criminal liability.

sources.publisher: U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee (Democratic press release)
sources.title: Senators Call for Investigation of Trump's Dealings with Corrupt Oligarch Linked to Iran

facts.claim: Global Witness reported in November 2017 that units at the Trump Ocean Club in Panama, a project to which the Trump Organization licensed its name and provided management, were bought through intermediaries by Colombian David Murcia Guzmán, later convicted in the United States of laundering drug money, and estimated the Trump Organization may have collected up to $75.4 million in licensing and management fees. The Trump Organization said it had no involvement in the sale of units.
facts.quote: The same report estimated that the Trump Organization may have collected as much as $75,400,000 from the Trump Ocean Club through its licensing and management fees.

sources.title: Narco-a-lago: Money Laundering at the Trump Ocean Club, Panama
Donald Trump made millions from selling his name to a Panama development used to launder drug money
A Panama tower carries Trump's name and ties to organized crime

facts.claim: NBC News and Reuters reported that Brazilian broker Alexandre Ventura Nogueira handled between one-third and one-half of advance unit sales at the Trump Ocean Club; Nogueira was arrested in Panama in 2009 on unrelated fraud charges, fled while on bail, and told NBC he had participated in money laundering unrelated to the building project. In March 2018 Rep. Norma Torres and colleagues wrote to U.S. agencies about the project, noting a Brazilian money-laundering investigation of Nogueira, which he denied.
facts.quote: Reuters found that Brazilian Alexandre Ventura Nogueira was responsible for between one-third and one-half of advance sales for the project.

sources.title: A Panama tower carries Trump's name and ties to organized crime
Trump Ocean Club Panama: Torres, Engel press Drug Enforcement
Narco-a-lago: Money Laundering at the Trump Ocean Club, Panama

connections.claim: Dar Global is the Trump Organization's development partner for Trump Tower Jeddah (launched December 2024), Trump International Hotel & Tower Dubai (April 2025), the Simaisma golf club and villas in Qatar (April 2025), Trump Plaza Jeddah (September 2025) and the Diriyah golf project near Riyadh (January 2026).
connections.quote: the fifth collaboration between DarGlobal and the Trump Organisation

sources.title: DarGlobal and The Trump Organization Launch Dubai's New Icon, Trump International Hotel & Tower
Dar Global and Trump Organisation launch luxury project in Riyadh's Diriyah

connections.quote: the company was established in 2005 by the Qatar Investment Authority

sources.title: About Qatari Diar
Qatari Diar Signs Strategic Agreement with Dar Global to Develop Trump International Golf Club and Trump Villas

connections.claim: The Trump Organization leased the federally owned Old Post Office building in Washington from the General Services Administration for 60 years and operated it as the Trump International Hotel until selling the lease in 2022; the sale required GSA approval.
connections.quote: The sale must first be approved by the General Services Administration, the federal agency that controls the property.

sources.title: CGI Merchant Group purchases Trump hotel in DC; expected to remove Trump name

connections.claim: The Trump Organization sold the lease on the Trump International Hotel Washington to Miami-based CGI Merchant Group, agreeing the deal in November 2021 and completing it in May 2022 at a reported $375 million.
connections.quote: The Trump Organization said Wednesday it had completed the sale of the Trump International Hotel to CGI Merchant Group of Miami

sources.title: Trump Organization Completes $375 million Sale of D.C. Hotel

connections.claim: A Trump Organization affiliate was a joint-venture partner with Bayrock Group and the Sapir Organization in Trump SoHo, with Trump licensing his name for an 18 percent equity stake.
connections.quote: Trump SoHo itself was a joint venture of Bayrock, the Sapir Organization, and a Trump Organization affiliate.

sources.title: How Russian Money Boosted Trump's Business Empire
Trump SoHo: A Shiny Hotel Wrapped In Glass, But Hiding Mysteries

connections.claim: In 2010 the Trump Organization engaged Felix Sater for about six months to prospect for real-estate deals, with Trump Organization business cards describing him as a senior adviser to Donald Trump.
connections.quote: Sater's role was to prospect for high-end real estate deals for the Trump Organization. The arrangement lasted six months, Garten said.

sources.title: Top Trump business adviser admitted role in mafia-linked stock fraud scheme

openQuestions: The Trump Organization's own release on the Qatar project names only Dar Global as its partner, while Qatari Diar's release names both Qatari Diar and Dar Global; the contractual relationship between the Trump Organization and Qatari Diar (licensing vs. direct agreement) should be checked in the releases themselves.

No source reached states a direct relationship between the Trump Organization and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund; Dar Global's ownership (reported as a London-listed arm of Dar Al Arkan) was not verified and no PIF connection is recorded.

The task referred to an Air Force statement in July 2025; the Air & Space Forces Magazine article recording the 'Executive Airlift support' statement is undated in the search result, so the item carries the 2026 statements' dates. The owner should confirm the July 2025 date on the page.
Whether the Justice Department memo on the aircraft was released to Congress, and whether the plane was transferred to the presidential library foundation as reported, were not confirmed.
Dollar values for the Qatar project ($3 billion, Siasat) and the Saudi projects ($10 billion, Reuters via The National) come from press reports, not the companies.

The ProPublica PPP articles themselves (July and December 2020) were not reachable; the PPP items rely on NBC's analysis as relayed by The Hill and Newsweek, and on PolitiFact's summary of ProPublica.
No source reached ties any 2020-21 pardon to the entities on this site, so no pardon items are recorded for the first term.
The GSA lease start date is given as 2012 (award) by CNN and 2013 (lease) by AFP; the GSA record should be checked.

The original New Yorker article (newyorker.com) is blocked to the crawler; the Baku facts rest on NPR's summary and a reprint. Reuters' Panama investigation is likewise cited through NBC and Global Witness; the Trump Organization's full response should be checked at the source.
